findings: Formatter callbacks and write/flush/close public interfaces return void, so write-result propagation must be inspected explicitly rather than inferred from API.
Output files opened with fopen(w) during formatter addition; existing output can be truncated before traversal begins. Optional backup renames regular files only.
Backup rename failure only logged and function returns void; add continues to fopen(w), so requested backup failure is not a local guard against overwriting old output.
Handler clone copies full template including mutex then code initializes original template mutex rather than copied mutex. Actual GLib mutex initialization/lifetime effects require runtime control.
rm_fmt_clear removes handler/file table entries with handler free but no file-handle close in inspected path. Full close logic remains unread.
Output path resolved after opening; identity exclusion vs alias/hardlink cases still to inspect. No atomic output replacement or durable-write protocol in this addition path.
